key_insight: Light can reversibly switch halide ions in 2D mixed-halide perovskites through intrinsic light–lattice coupling, not defects, enabling a self-resetting optical response.
engineering_relevance: This points to defect-free, photo-tunable perovskite devices with reversible optical switching for adaptive photonics and optoelectronics.
method: Nudged elastic band calculations to map the halide-exchange activation path.
Photo-force calculations to quantify non-equilibrium light-induced work on ions.
GW and lattice-dynamics/phonon analysis to connect band-gap, excitations, and soft modes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reproduction of the experimentally observed dark optical absorption spectra with GW and a light-induced redshift consistent with bandgap renormalization.
watch_item: The switching appears partial under illumination because photo-induced work does not fully overcome the ground-state barrier, so real-device performance may depend on light intensity and stability of the excited state.
paper_title: Reversible photo-switching optical functionality in two-dimensional mixed-halide hybrid perovskites
